# Wordpress (`wordpress-wordpress`)

Power your site with WordPress – the core behind 40% of the web. Enjoy seamless installation, robust customization, and unmatched scalability. Elevate your online presence effortlessly today!

[Service documentation](https://docs.osaas.io/osaas.wiki/Service%3A-Wordpress.html) · [Source](https://github.com/WordPress/WordPress)

## Example

```terraform
resource "osc_instance" "example" {
  service_id = "wordpress-wordpress"
  name       = "mywordpress"

  parameters = {
    DbHost        = "..."
    DbUser        = "..."
    DbPassword    = "..."
    # DbName        = "..."
    # DbTablePrefix = "..."
  }
}
```

Commented lines are optional parameters. Values marked `"..."` need a real value. Outputs are `url`, `external_ip`, `external_port` and the raw `instance` document, see the `osc_instance` resource.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DbHost` | string | yes | Hostname or IP address for the service |
| `DbUser` | string | yes | Database connection configuration |
| `DbPassword` | string | yes | Database connection configuration |
| `DbName` | string | no | Database connection configuration |
| `DbTablePrefix` | string | no | Configuration option for dbtableprefix |

The instance `name` must match `^\w+$` and be unique per service within the workspace. OSC lowercases it and allows at most 20 characters.

Parameter values are strings; booleans take `"true"` or `"false"`. Reference an `osc_secret` as `osc_secret.<name>.ref` to keep a value out of the instance configuration. This page is generated from the OSC catalog; the provider validates against the live catalog when planning.
